title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (section 6 of the notes). M^* = ⊕_{0≤i≤2n} M^i is a graded module, finite-dimensional over Q, standing in for H^*(X) with n = dim X. L is a degree-2 operator satisfying hard Lefschetz: L^{n-i}: M^i → M^{2n-i} is an isomorphism. Σ ⊂ End(M) is a graded subring standing in for the algebraic correspondences; it contains L and the Künneth projectors π_i. The previous page sets up the following:
- Primitive decomposition M^i = ⊕_α L^α P^{i-2α}.
- π_{iα} is the projector of M^i onto L^α P^{i-2α}.
- w_k (written W_k here) is the inverse of L^{n-k}: M^k → M^{2n-k}, extended by zero.
- (6.9) expresses π_{iα} through L, w and the higher π_{iα'}; (6.10) gives π_{2n-i,α} = L^{n-i} π_{iα} w_i.
The aim is to prove (iii), Λ ∈ Σ, assuming the w's lie in Σ. By (6.11), Λ = Σ_{j,α} Λπ_{jα}, so it suffices to show each Λπ_{jα} ∈ Σ.

On this page, for i ≤ n:
- (6.12): Λπ_{i0} = 0 and Λπ_{iα} = L^{α-1} W_{i-2α} L^{n-i+α} π_{iα} for α ≥ 1. The 'L' was corrected to L^{α-1}.
- (6.13), for i ≤ n-1: Λπ_{2n-i,α} = L^{n-i+α-1} W_{i-2α} L^α π_{2n-i,α}.

Check. Take p ∈ P^k with k = i-2α. In low degree, L^{n-i+α} sends L^α p to L^{n-k} p, W_k returns p, and L^{α-1} gives L^{α-1} p. In high degree the element is L^{n-i+α} p; L^α sends it to L^{n-k} p, W_k returns p, and L^{n-i+α-1} gives L^{n-i+α-1} p. So uniformly Λ(L^β p) = L^{β-1} p for β ≥ 1, and Λp = 0.

This Λ is NOT the sl2 Λ, which carries the factors β(n-k-β+1). It is the 'normalized' Λ, defined without denominators. It equals *^{-1} L * up to sign, as in Kleiman 1968 and Grothendieck's Bombay 1968 talk. It is characterized on the next page, (6.15), by
- LΛ = 1 − Σ_{i≤n} π_{i0},
- ΛL = 1 − Σ_{j≥n} π_{j0},
where π_{2n-i,0} is the projector onto L^{n-i} P^i, the top piece of each Lefschetz string. Since each w_k is a product of L's and Λ's, the conditions envisaged give Λ, π_{iα} ∈ Σ, hence (iv).

Grothendieck then poses the converse: does (iv) (all π_{iα} ∈ Σ) imply (ii) (the inverses w ∈ Σ, a Lefschetz-type condition)? He reduces it to showing π_i = π'_i, a comparison of two families of projectors from earlier pages, and writes 'Démonstration à fournir'.

Remark (6.14): a system of identities determining Λ ∈ Σ^{(-2)} and π_{iα} ∈ Σ^{(0)} uniquely in terms of L and the π_i alone. Here i ≤ n throughout.
- ① and ②: Λ^{n-i} L^{n-i} = 1 on M^i and L^{n-i} Λ^{n-i} = 1 on M^{2n-i}. So Λ^{n-k} restricted to M^{2n-k} equals W_k: inversion is expressed by Λ.
- ③: the recursion (6.9) with W replaced by Λ^{n-k}.
- ④: (6.10) rewritten.
- ⑤–⑦: (6.12) and (6.13) with W replaced by Λ powers.
- ⑧: Λ = Σ Λπ_{jα}.
The text then says ⑤–⑧ can be replaced by the two identities (6.15). Since the π_i are themselves intrinsic in the graded ring Σ, this gives a presentation of the 'Lefschetz' structure purely inside the graded ring Σ with L. That prepares section 7, the universal integral algebra Φ_0 = Z[L_0, Λ_0] acting on the exterior algebra of a unimodular symplectic lattice.
errors: In (6.14)③ the factor (1 − Σ_{α'>α} π_{i,α'}) should be (π_i − Σ_{α'>α} π_{i,α'}), or must be read as acting on M^i. Applied to all of M, the right-hand side is not supported on M^i. The same implicit restriction to M^i underlies (6.9).
In (6.14)⑦ the side condition is written 'si α ≤ n−1'. Mathematically it should be 'si i ≤ n−1', as in (6.13); for i = n the case is already covered by ⑥.
The Λ used here (Λ L^β p = L^{β−1} p) differs from the sl2/Hodge Λ by nonzero integer scalars on each L^β P^k. Not an error, but the identities (6.15) hold only for this normalized Λ.

Possible inconsistency, from the next page's transcription (uncertain reading): the contraction Λ_0 = ξ_0^*⌟ on the exterior algebra of a symplectic lattice is the sl2-normalized Λ. It does not satisfy (6.15), so identifying it with 'the canonical operation defined by (6.15)' would be inaccurate.
The claim that (iv) implies (ii) is left unproved ('Démonstration à fournir'), and the reduction to π_i = π'_i is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Explicit formulas Λπ_{iα} = L^{α−1} w_{i−2α} L^{n−i+α} π_{iα}, and the analogue in degrees 2n−i, showing Λ is algebraic once the Lefschetz inverses are
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of the Lefschetz standard conjecture forms B(X) ⇔ Λ algebraic ⇔ inverse of L^{n−i} algebraic
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay Colloquium 1968, publ. 1969); Kleiman 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968)

ideas.what: Normalized (denominator-free) Λ with Λ L^β p = L^{β−1} p, characterized by LΛ = 1 − Σ_{i≤n} π_{i0}, ΛL = 1 − Σ_{j≥n} π_{j0}
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Kleiman Λ operator (= *^{-1} L * up to sign), as opposed to the sl2 Λ
ideas.where_published: Bombay 1968 standard conjectures paper (Λ operator); Kleiman 1968 §1.4

ideas.what: A complete system of ring-theoretic identities (6.14) determining Λ and all primitive-decomposition projectors π_{iα} uniquely from L and the Künneth projectors inside the abstract graded ring Σ
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic algebraic characterization of the Lefschetz (sl2-type) structure in a graded endomorphism algebra; Lefschetz decomposition projectors as elements of the correspondence algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kleiman (primitive decomposition projectors algebraic under B); Kahn–Murre–Pedrini / Künnemann for Lefschetz-decomposition of motives
ideas.where_published: Not as a system of relations; the published Bombay paper only states the B ⇔ Λ algebraic equivalences

ideas.what: Question whether algebraicity of all Lefschetz-decomposition projectors π_{iα} (condition iv) implies the Lefschetz condition (ii)
ideas.modern_name: Relation between algebraicity of the refined (primitive) Künneth/Lefschetz projectors and the Lefschetz standard conjecture B
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not clearly addressed as such; B ⇒ C (Kleiman) is the known direction

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether algebraicity of all primitive-decomposition projectors π_{iα} implies the Lefschetz-type condition (ii) (inverses of L^{n−i} algebraic, i.e. B). He reduces it to an identity π_i = π'_i and leaves it open. The literature treats B ⇒ (projectors algebraic) but, to my knowledge, does not isolate this converse question in this form.
missed.quote: je ne sais pas si (iv) implique (ii). Il suffit de prouver en fait que l'on a alors π_i=π'_i. Démonstration à fournir.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a potentially weaker-looking hypothesis equivalent (or not) to B. Algebraicity of refined Lefschetz-decomposition projectors arises in work on Chow–Künneth/Lefschetz decompositions of motives (Murre, Künnemann, Kahn–Murre–Pedrini). An answer, even in the abstract setting of a graded algebra with L, would clarify the logical position of B. In the abstract setting a counterexample may well exist, and settling it is a small but clean question.

missed.claim: The deliberate use of the denominator-free Λ, characterized by LΛ = 1 − Σπ_{i0}, ΛL = 1 − Σπ_{j0}, is motivated here by an integral 'universal Lefschetz algebra' Φ_0 = Z[L_0, Λ_0] (section 7). This suggests Grothendieck intended a Z-structure on the Lefschetz algebra of correspondences. The published Bombay paper works over Q.
missed.quote: Voici un système de conditions déterminant de façon unique les éléments Λ∈Σ^{(-2)}, π_{i,α}∈Σ^{(0)} : en termes de L, et des π_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and torsion questions for the Lefschetz standard conjecture and integral motives are of current interest. The page shows only a minor, preparatory step, though.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine verification of the Λ ⇔ Lefschetz-inverse equivalence and of the normalized Λ, which appear in the Bombay 1968 paper and in Kleiman 1968. The only mildly notable items are the explicit open question whether algebraic primitive projectors imply B, and the ring-theoretic presentation (6.14) aimed at an integral universal Lefschetz algebra.
transcription_corrections: Lines 1–2: 'Or si i≤n, on aura' — correct.
(6.12): the second formula reads Λπ_{iα} = L^{α−1} W_{i−2α} L^{n−i+α} π_{iα}; the original 'L' is overwritten with exponent α−1. W is the same operator as w on the previous page.

(6.13): the exponent of L originally included '+α' crossed out, giving L^{n−i−1} W_{i−2α} L^α π_{2n−i,α}. By the later corrected ⑦ the intended exponent is n−i+α−1, so the crossed-out version is itself erroneous.
The phrase reads 'Les conditions envisagées impliquent évidemment (iv) ; je ne sais pas si (iv) implique (ii). Il suffit de prouver en fait que l'on a alors π_i=π'_i.'
In (6.14)⑦ the image appears to read 'si α ≤ n−1', but mathematically 'si i ≤ n−1' is meant.
In (6.14)③ the factor written L^α Λ^{n−i+2α} L^{n−i+α} is correct; the leading L^α overwrites an earlier attempt.
